verdict.rationale: pnpm's docs say node_modules files are hard-linked from a single content-addressable store, so a hundred projects on the same version cost one copy on disk. Updates add only changed files to the store, and offline installs can draw from it. Community users independently confirm the result: disk usage dropped dramatically and installs across projects are fast because packages are already on disk. Missing for 10: documentation of store management (store location, pruning/verification); one real-world report measured only ~30% disk savings, so the extent of savings varies.
